misconceptions.description: Believing adjective-only levels (Excellent, Good, Fair) can be scored consistently across raters
misconceptions.trigger: rubric levels use adjectives with no observable or countable anchor
misconceptions.feedback: Rewrite each level as observable counts or conditions so two raters look at the same evidence.

misconceptions.description: Treating averaging two scores to the midpoint as if it resolved a calibration disagreement
misconceptions.trigger: raters reconcile by taking a mean instead of finding what each was looking at
misconceptions.feedback: Read the disagreement: find which evidence each rater weighed differently, then fix the descriptor.

misconceptions.description: Counting rater agreement that came from shared habit rather than shared evidence anchors
misconceptions.trigger: raters agree but cannot point to the rubric language that produced the agreement
misconceptions.feedback: Trace the agreement to a specific descriptor; agreement without an anchor will not transfer to new drafts.
